name: Alfa Romeo 8C 2300 Corto Touring Spider 1932
description:
The Alfa Romeo 8C 2300 represents one of the most successful and beautiful racing sports cars of the early 1930s. Built between 1931 and 1934, the 8C 2300 dominated motorsport during its era, with victories at Le Mans, the Mille Miglia, the Targa Florio, and countless Grand Prix races.

The name '8C' refers to the eight-cylinder engine configuration - actually two inline-four cylinder blocks mounted back-to-back on a common crankcase, creating a straight-eight. The supercharged 2.3-liter engine produces 165 horsepower at 5400 RPM, with the Roots-type supercharger driven by gears from the center of the engine. This innovative layout allowed for exceptional mechanical efficiency and reliability.

The 'Corto' (short) chassis version presented here was bodied by the legendary Carrozzeria Touring with their elegant Spider design. Weighing just 990 kg and featuring advanced engineering for the period, the 8C 2300 could reach 185 km/h - extraordinary performance for 1932.

Racing legends like Tazio Nuvolari, Rudolf Caracciola, and Louis Chiron drove 8C 2300s to countless victories. Even Enzo Ferrari raced these cars before founding his own marque, taking second place at the Circuito delle Tre Provincie in 1931. The 8C's success cemented Alfa Romeo's reputation for building the world's finest sporting automobiles.

Today, the 8C 2300 is among the most valuable and desirable pre-war automobiles, representing the absolute pinnacle of 1930s racing car design.
